event.title: Swedish National Arrested in Russia, Accused of Leading Ukrainian Drone Unit
event.canonical_title: Swedish National Arrested in Russia, Accused of Leading Ukrainian Drone Unit
event.summary: Russian intelligence has arrested a Swedish man at the western border, alleging he led a Ukrainian drone unit. He faces accusations of planning acts of terrorism and sabotage. The arrest comes amid heightened tensions between Russia and Ukraine, with ongoing accusations from Russia regarding Ukraine's actions against US-brokered peace efforts.

event_overview.title: About Russia-Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.subject: Russia-Ukraine Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Russia-Ukraine conflict is an armed conflict centered on Ukraine that began with Russia’s occupation of Crimea and fighting in eastern Ukraine in 2014, then expanded sharply when Russian forces launched a full-scale attack on 24 February 2022. It has combined conventional military operations, occupation and territorial-control disputes, humanitarian consequences, and national and international criminal-law investigations.

facts.label: Origins and escalation
facts.value: Russia began occupying Ukrainian territory in Crimea in February 2014; armed conflict subsequently developed in parts of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. Russia launched its full-scale armed attack against Ukraine on 24 February 2022.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: The conflict concerns Ukraine’s internationally recognized territory, including Crimea and areas affected by hostilities or Russian occupation in the Donetsk, Kharkiv, Kherson, Luhansk, Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia regions.

facts.label: United Nations position
facts.value: In resolution ES-11/1, adopted on 2 March 2022, the UN General Assembly deplored Russia’s aggression against Ukraine and demanded that Russia cease its use of force and withdraw its military forces from Ukraine.

facts.label: International criminal-law process
facts.value: The International Criminal Court opened its Ukraine investigation on 2 March 2022 after referrals by States Parties. Its stated scope covers alleged war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide committed by any person on Ukrainian territory from 21 November 2013 onward.

facts.label: Humanitarian impact
facts.value: The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission has documented civilian deaths, injuries, displacement, and damage to homes, schools, health facilities and other civilian infrastructure resulting from the full-scale hostilities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights specific cross-border criminal or security cases involving foreign nationals allegedly joining or assisting either side; it does not provide a complete record of battlefield developments, diplomacy, humanitarian conditions, or all conflict-related prosecutions.
